Every target is checked before anything is written. A note whose target is missing is fatal:
something was renamed or removed upstream. So is an addition whose target now EXISTS: Synchra
documented it, and ours should be deleted rather than shadow theirs.
Prose is Markdown and ends up in a generated client's docblocks, so keep it to what a caller
needs at the call site. Facts about the document itself stay in docs/CAVEATS.md.
Everything factual here was verified against the live service, not inferred from the document.
info: **Notes below this line are not from Synchra.** They were added by
https://github.com/Bluscream/synchra-api, which also carries the per-endpoint notes, the
TikTok gift tables, and the caveats that have no endpoint to hang on.
**There is no token endpoint.** `OAuth2` is declared with an empty `flows` object and there is no
authorize or token URL anywhere in the API. Tokens are issued from the dashboard by hand and sent
as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. In particular `POST /api/2/auth/token` does not exist and
answers 404, so a refresh-grant flow cannot be built; resolve the token from outside the process.
**Scopes are not the same thing as access.** A token carries a fixed scope set, and whether it
may act on a given channel is granted separately, per channel. A 403 therefore does not
necessarily mean a missing scope.
**A good part of the API is public.** Operations with `security: []` were each verified to answer
without a token. The rest answer 401 without one.
**Error responses are documented by this overlay, not by Synchra.** The published description
lists only successes and 422, though 401, 403, 404 and 429 all occur. Every error body is the
`Error` schema — `{code, message, type, errors[]}` — which was confirmed against live responses.
**Do not retry POST or PATCH automatically.** The API rate-limits with 429 and sends
`Retry-After`, but offers no idempotency key, so a retried POST that had already succeeded sends
the message twice. GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT and DELETE are safe to retry.
**Two credential types exist that are not security schemes.** A channel ingest API key is passed
as an ordinary parameter, and the widget `x-kv-token` header is declared below as `WidgetKvToken`.

OAuth2.description: Kept with the empty `flows` the service publishes, because every operation's `security` refers to it by name and removing it would leave those references dangling. There is no OAuth2 flow in practice: a token is created in the dashboard and sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. See `BearerToken`, which describes what actually happens on the wire.

BearerToken.description: How a token is really sent. Added by synchra-api: the published description has no scheme for it.

WidgetKvToken.name: x-kv-token
WidgetKvToken.description: Authorises writes to a widget's shared key-value store. Added by synchra-api; it appears in no published security scheme.

get.description:
> Added by https://github.com/Bluscream/synchra-api — the service answers this, the published description does not list it.

Liveness check. Needs no credential.

It *was* in the description as of 2026-04-02 and has since been removed from it — but not from the service, which still answers 200. Verified live.

> Added by https://github.com/Bluscream/synchra-api — the published description does not list this route.

The realtime gateway: `wss://api.synchra.net/api/2/ws`. Omitted from the OpenAPI document because OpenAPI 3.1 cannot describe a socket; the protocol is specified in `spec/websocket.md`, served by `GET /api/2/ws-docs`.

It is listed here so that a reader of the description knows the gateway exists and where it is.

**The handshake itself takes no credential** — verified: a plain `GET` answers `426 Upgrade Required`, not 401. The socket is authenticated *after* connecting, by sending an `authorization` command; private subscriptions fail until then.

The socket accepts the bare text `ping` as well as `{"command":"ping"}` and replies with the bare text `pong` — not JSON. A client that pipes every frame through a JSON parser will throw on its own keepalive.

101.description: Switching protocols; the connection becomes a WebSocket.

426.description: Sent for a plain request with no `Connection: Upgrade` header. The body is a plain-text protocol-violation message, not an `Error`.

KvEventData.title: KvEventData
KvEventData.description:
> Added by https://github.com/Bluscream/synchra-api.

The payload of a `widget_value` gateway event: one key in a widget's shared key-value store changed. Named by `spec/websocket.md`, which defines no schema for it; these fields follow its documented example.

value.title: Value
value.description: Any JSON value. Genuinely unconstrained — do not model it as a union.

ChannelGiveawaysEventData.title: ChannelGiveawaysEventData
ChannelGiveawaysEventData.description:
> Added by https://github.com/Bluscream/synchra-api.

The payload of a `channel_giveaways` gateway event: a pointer, not the giveaway. Re-read the giveaway to get its new state. Named by `spec/websocket.md`, which defines no schema for it.

QueueEvent.title: QueueEvent
QueueEvent.description:
> Added by https://github.com/Bluscream/synchra-api.

The payload of a `channel_queue` gateway event. It carries only the kind of change, for example `channel_queue_viewer_created` — re-read the queue to get its contents. Named by `spec/websocket.md`, which defines no schema for it.

ActivityAlertWidgetTest.title: ActivityAlertWidgetTest
ActivityAlertWidgetTest.description:
> Added by https://github.com/Bluscream/synchra-api.

The payload of an `activity_alert_test` gateway event: a test alert fired at one widget, carrying a whole activity. Present in `spec/websocket.md` as a JSON example only — no schema, not even a named type reference.

429.description: Rate limited. Carries `Retry-After`. Added by synchra-api; the published description documents no error but 422.

500.description: Server error. Added by synchra-api; the published description documents no error but 422.

401.description: No token, or a token the service does not accept. Body is an `Error` with `type: unauthenticated`. Added by synchra-api, verified against the live service.

403.description: Authenticated but not permitted. Usually means the token is not granted on this channel rather than that a scope is missing — the two are separate. Added by synchra-api, verified against the live service.

404.description: No such route, or no such resource. Note that a *list* endpoint given an unknown parent id answers 200 with an empty `records` array instead of 404. Added by synchra-api, verified against the live service.

GET /api/2/channels/{channel_id}/activit: **A 403 here usually means the token is not granted on this channel, not that a scope is
missing.** Holding `channel_activity:read` is necessary and not sufficient: per-channel access
is granted separately, in the dashboard. A token minted by one account for another account's
channel reads chat happily and refuses this.
Needs a token — verified: an anonymous call answers 401. Note that a gift, sub or raid does
GET /api/2/channels/{channel_id}/chat-me: **Public** — verified to answer without a token.
Carries gifts, subs and raids as well as chat, as *notices*. A notice leaves `message_parts`
empty and puts its content in `notice_message_parts` instead, so a reader that looks only at
`message_parts` renders every gift as a blank row. See the `ChatMessage` schema.
A TikTok gift identifies itself with `type: notice`, `sub_type: tiktok_gift`. To turn a gift
into a price or a localised name, see the tables in
https://github.com/Bluscream/synchra-api/tree/main/data — the API offers no lookup for them.
An unknown `channel_id` answers **200 with an empty `records` array**, not 404. Do not use this
to test whether a channel exists.
GET /api/2/channels/{channel_id}/chat-ev: **Public** — verified to answer without a token.
GET /api/2/channels/{channel_id}/random-: **Public** — verified to answer without a token.
GET /api/2/channels/{channel_id}/provide: **Public** — verified to answer without a token. With `provider-streams`, this is enough to
build a live-status page with no credentials at all.
GET /api/2/channels/{channel_id}: Needs a token, unlike the channel's `providers`, `provider-streams` and chat — verified: an
anonymous call answers 401. A public page that only needs the display name and live state can
GET /api/2/channels/{channel_id}/viewers: **The only reliable source of a viewer's picture.** `viewer_profile_picture_url` on a chat
message is filled for some providers and null for others, so a chat log rendered straight from
the API shows avatars for some people and blanks for the rest. This endpoint has one for every
It is one request per viewer, so do not call it while rendering. Cache per **viewer** rather
than per message — somebody talking twenty times should cost one lookup — and cache the
negative answer too, or every refresh retries everyone who has not set a picture.
Needs a token that can read this channel's viewers; without that it answers 403.
GET /api/2/channels/{channel_id}/provide: **Public** — verified to answer without a token. Carries status, title, `viewer_count`,
GET /api/2/widgets/{widget_id}: **Public, and the `widget_id` is the capability.** There is no further authorisation on a
widget: anyone holding the id can read it. Treat one like a secret — do not put it in a page
that is served to viewers if the widget's contents are not meant for them.
POST /api/2/chat/messages: **Not safe to retry.** No idempotency key is offered, so a retry of a request that had already
succeeded posts the message a second time. If you wrap this in a retry policy, exclude it.
GET /api/2/ws-docs: Answers with the WebSocket protocol reference as Markdown — about 61 KB. The published
description repeats that entire document inside this operation's own `description`, which is
the only `description` Synchra fills anywhere in the API.
A generator should treat it as a document to link to, not text to inline: it is 2,000+ lines of
GET /api/2/chat/emotes: Needs a token — verified: an anonymous call answers 401. That is worth knowing because the
chat messages these emotes decorate are *public*, so a public chat renderer can show the text
but cannot resolve the emote list from here.
In practice it does not need to: a chat message's `message_parts` already carry each emote's
CDN urls at three sizes, so nothing has to be looked up.

Error: The body of every error response, confirmed against the live service for 401, 404 and 422:
`type` is a stable machine-readable string — `unauthenticated`, `validation_error` — except on a
routing 404, where it is the **empty string**. Branch on `code` first.
`errors` carries per-field detail for a 422 and is an empty array otherwise.
The published description references this schema only from 422 responses. Every other error
response in this document was added by synchra-api.
SubError: One field's validation failure, inside `Error.errors`. `input` is the value that was rejected
and may be any JSON type, or null.
`field` is the parameter or body field name — for a query parameter the service reports it
ChatMessage: **A notice carries its content somewhere else.** Normally the rendered content is the ordered,
typed list in `message_parts`. For a notice — a gift, a sub, a raid — `message_parts` is
**empty** and the content is in `notice_message_parts` instead.
Reading only `message_parts` therefore draws every gift as a blank row, and because gifts
cluster, a busy stream's chat log appears to go dead. Read whichever list is non-empty.
Deciding whether a notice counts as a "message" or an "event" in your own UI is worth doing
deliberately: the API delivers it through `chat-messages`, not through `activities`, so a
notification filter split along those lines puts gifts on the chat side.
ChatMessage.viewer_profile_picture_url: **Present for some providers, null for others** — filled for TikTok, not for Twitch or
YouTube. Do not treat an absence as "this viewer has no picture"; it usually means Synchra
did not resolve one. The picture is available from
ChatMessage.viewer_name: A handle, not a URL — the API carries no link to a viewer's profile, and building one is
per-provider. YouTube is addressed by channel id (`provider_viewer_id`), everyone else by
handle, and some providers have no public profile page at all.
ChatMessagePart: Everything needed to render is already here: an `emote` carries its CDN urls at three sizes,
a `gift` an image url, a `mention` the resolved display name, a `link` its url. No second
lookup is required. Each part also has a text fallback, so a renderer that ignores images
ChatMessage.notice_message_parts: The content of a notice — a gift, a sub, a raid. When this is non-empty, `message_parts` is
**empty**, and this is what there is to render.
Activity.message_parts: Unlike `ChatMessage`, an activity has no second `notice_message_parts` list; this is always
Activity.viewer_profile_picture_url: As on `ChatMessage`: filled for some providers and null for others, so an absence does not
mean the viewer has no picture.
GiftPart: **A gift already carries everything needed to render it.** `name`, `image_url`, `count` and
`count_display_name` all arrive resolved, so nothing has to be looked up — in particular you do
not need a gift table to turn an id into a name or a picture. Observed live:
Three things about it are not obvious.
**`name` is in whatever language the platform sent, which varies within one channel.** The sample
above is German (`Imperator Herz`) and arrived alongside `Popular Vote`, `Heart Me` and `Rose` in
English, on the same channel. There is no parameter to ask for a locale. If you need consistent
language you must translate it yourself — and see below, because the obvious way does not work.
**`id` is Synchra's cross-platform gift identifier, not TikTok's catalogue id.** Non-TikTok gifts
use string ids (`rose`, `super_chat`, `cheer-1000`) and the TikTok ones do not reliably match the
ids in a scraped gift table: of five sampled, one matched. Do not join on it without checking.
**`count` and the part's `text` do not mean one fixed thing.** Across one sample: `count: 1` with
text `"1 diamond"`, `count: 10` with text `"10 diamonds"`, `count: 10` with text `"Tiny Diny"`,
and `count: 10000000` with text `"$10.00"` for a YouTube Super Chat. Read `type` and
`count_display_name` before interpreting `count` as a price, a quantity or a currency amount.
